checks.note: signUpload's PutObjectPresignRequest signs only bucket/key/contentType (no length), and no read path re-HEADs: confirmUpload stores head.contentLength() once, reconfirm returns the stale row, and signDownload/findActiveObject/sumSizeBytesByOwnerId all trust DB sizeBytes while signedDownloadUrl serves whatever is in S3. A second PUT with the still-valid URL (irrevocable by design; content-length-range applies only to POST policies, not presigned PUT) overwrites the object unchecked.

reconfirm's only gate before re-publishing StorageObjectConfirmedEvent is the time-window check on fso.getUploadConfirmedAt() (confirmedAt.isAfter(now - uploadTtlSeconds)); re-confirming older upload A within the TTL after B passes it and re-fires A's event, and the method's own javadoc/comment say listeners unconditionally set the field to the event's key, so photo_url reverts to A. The window shrinks but does not prevent the race.

matches.note: R2 states confirmUpload trusts the client-declared Content-Type and never reads the stored bytes, allowing arbitrary content (HTML, executables) to be stored under an image type — same defect, place, and consequence.
No reported finding mentions that rejected confirms (validation/quota failures) leave the already-PUT object in the bucket uncounted and uncleaned.
R3 mentions the allowlist accepting application/octet-stream only as context; no finding flags the FileStorageProperties defaults (octet-stream/.bin) as the defect to fix.
No reported finding addresses signUpload accepting arbitrary entity strings with ownership checked only for OWNER_BOUND_ENTITIES.
R4 identifies that saveStep5 only prefix-checks photoUrl and never verifies a confirmed, non-deleted, owned, image-typed object, including the ".." suffix case — same defect and consequence.
